title: Observability housekeeping: async exporters, sensible sampling, and lightweight logging shim
creator: Diego Liu
description: Problem: Several services have grown heavy observability overhead from synchronous logging, blocking metric exporters, and older OpenTelemetry SDKs that allocate frequently. This increases tail latency and raises cost on high-throughput RPC paths. Goal: reduce CPU and latency impact of telemetry while preserving fidelity for SLOs and incident debugging. Scope: 1) Upgrade OpenTelemetry SDKs to latest stable in Go and Python flavors, 2) Replace synchronous metric/log exporters with async background workers (bounded queues + backpressure), 3) Introduce safer default sampling (adaptive parent-based + 1% default) with a per-route override, 4) Replace large logging dependency with a small shim that supports structured logs and non-blocking drains, 5) Add metrics for telemetry self-cost (telemetry_cpu_pct, telemetry_queue_size, telemetry_dropped_spans). Acceptance criteria: - End-to-end p50/p99 request latency on gateway and tokenizer services improves or stays within 5% of baseline under peak synthetic load, - Telemetry CPU consumption reduces by at least 20% in high-throughput scenarios, - No loss of critical traces for 99% of sampled error requests, - Canary rollout plan and automated rollback for any error spike. Implementation plan: - Phase A (this ticket): implement async exporter framework and logging shim in go-common, add SDK upgrade compatibility layer and metric/exporter wrappers, add feature flag to enable new sampler and exporter per service. Create unit and integration tests that simulate exporter slowdowns and verify bounded queue behavior. - Phase B: incrementally flip services (gateway -> tokenizer -> runtime pods) in canary batches, monitor telemetry_self_cost metrics and request SLOs. - Rollout: use Console rollout pipeline with canary 5% -> 25% -> 100% over 72 hours with automatic fallback if error rate increases > 0.5% absolute or latency p99 regresses > 10%. Testing and validation: load test script in repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability-loadtests/tree/ENG-21034, PRs will include benchmark artifacts (flamegraphs, allocation diffs). Risks: losing trace fidelity for rare errors if sampling overly aggressive; mitigated by prioritized sampling for errors and a short-term increase in sampling on rollback. Notes: keep exporters pluggable to support Dedicated and Private deployment constraints (local KMS/gateways).

2026-02-28 Priya Nair: Design review done with Platform and Runtime teams. Agreed on bounded queue size 4096 and backpressure strategy = drop oldest when full + counter metric. Added structured metric names to doc.

2026-03-03 Nathan Cole (review): Concern around sampling defaults for enterprise customers. Action: add per-tenant override in config and preserve 100% sampling for requests tagged with compliance-level:high.

2026-03-07 Diego Liu: Integration tests added to CI. Found a race in exporter shutdown path; fixed by adding drain timeout and context cancel semantics. Patch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/go-common/pull/518

2026-03-10 Priya Nair: Started canary on gateway (5%). Observability_self_cost metrics look stable; one pod saw a transient 0.6% error bump attributed to a misconfigured sampler rule. Rolled back that pod and pushed config fix.
